v.why: Replacing a missing edge with a 3x3 conv adds a learnable path, as in experiment 8 (+3.1/+6.2/+8.0), while replacing an existing op gains less.
Swapping a parameter-free pool for a conv gives a large gain, as in experiment 14 (+3.9/+8.7/+6.9).
Replacing the first-layer conv with a pool cuts accuracy sharply on all datasets, as in experiments 9 and 13.
Pooling in place of a 3x3 conv on the input edge loses a lot of capacity, as in experiment 12 (-4.6/-7.4/-9.7).
Removing an existing pool edge hurts on all three datasets, as in experiment 7, and removing it is worse than removing a skip.
Deleting the conv on the output edge costs accuracy on all three datasets, as in experiment 16, which is worse than editing an edge that is already weak.
Replacing the direct-to-output 3x3 conv with a skip loses a lot of capacity, as in experiment 3 (-7.4/-6.6/-9.9).
Downgrading the input-edge 3x3 conv to a skip hurts on all three datasets, as in experiment 1.
Adding a conv where the edge was missing yields a gain, as in experiment 15, unlike replacing an existing conv.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on the intermediate edge removes a useful path, whereas removing an already weak op costs little.
